security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around commands, filenames, and field names rather than executable backtick syntax. The real concern is workflow safety: the skill documents destructive Kapso and WhatsApp automation actions without explicit confirmation guardrails.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before create, update, delete, deploy, force status, resume, or database mutation actions. Include the target workflow, account, function, integration, or table in the confirmation.

remediation.issue: Sensitive Kapso credential guidance is minimal.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to keep KAPSO_API_KEY in environment variables, use least-privilege keys where possible, avoid pasting secrets into prompts, and rotate shared keys.

remediation.issue: Referenced helper scripts are not included in the scanned package.
remediation.suggestion: Package the referenced scripts or clearly state the trusted repository and setup steps before asking users to run commands.

content.value_statement: WhatsApp automation changes can be hard to coordinate across triggers, workflows, functions, and data. This skill gives structured Kapso workflow steps and command references for agent-assisted updates.
actual_capabilities: Provides steps to fetch, validate, edit, and update Kapso workflow graphs.
Documents WhatsApp trigger listing, creation, toggling, deletion, and phone number lookup.
Guides execution debugging with execution details, context values, and event history.
Explains how to create, deploy, verify, invoke, and inspect project functions.
Shows how to find apps, accounts, actions, schemas, and integration records.
Lists database table, query, create, update, upsert, and delete workflows.
limitations: Requires a Kapso account, WhatsApp setup, API base URL, and KAPSO_API_KEY.
Requires local Kapso helper scripts and dependencies before commands can run.
Cannot bypass Kapso, WhatsApp, OAuth, or database permission controls.
Destructive operations need human review before production execution.

use_cases.title: Build Inbound Support Automation
use_cases.description: Create and adjust a WhatsApp workflow that receives messages, routes users, and starts support handling.

use_cases.title: Debug Conversation Failures
use_cases.description: Inspect recent executions, read context values, and review event history to find broken workflow steps.

use_cases.title: Connect Apps and Data
use_cases.description: Configure action integrations, deploy workflow functions, and use database rows for workflow state.

prompt_templates.title: Find My Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: List my Kapso workflows and identify the one that handles inbound WhatsApp support. Summarize the likely workflow purpose before suggesting changes.

prompt_templates.title: Add a WhatsApp Trigger
prompt_templates.scenario: Set up message intake with approval before mutation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the WhatsApp phone number ID for this account, then prepare an inbound message trigger for workflow WORKFLOW_ID. Ask for my confirmation before creating it.

prompt_templates.title: Edit and Validate a Graph
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch workflow WORKFLOW_ID, explain its current graph, add a decision branch for VIP customers, validate the graph, and ask before updating it with the lock version.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Integrated Agent Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with function, app integration, and data lookup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a WhatsApp support workflow that checks a D1 table, calls an app action through an agent node, and deploys a helper function. Show each planned mutation before execution.

output_examples.input: Inspect the latest failed execution for my WhatsApp support workflow.
output_examples.output: The workflow has one recent failed execution. The failure occurred after the routing step because the expected customer tier value was missing. Recommended next step: inspect the context path and confirm whether the table lookup returned a row.

output_examples.input: Add an inbound WhatsApp trigger to workflow 123.
output_examples.output: I found the available WhatsApp phone numbers and prepared the trigger details for workflow 123. This will create a new inbound trigger, so I will wait for your explicit approval before running the create step.

output_examples.input: Review my graph update before deployment.
output_examples.output: The updated graph keeps the original node IDs, adds one decision branch, and preserves the existing start node. Validation should run before update, and the final update needs the current lock version.

best_practices: Confirm every production create, update, delete, deploy, force, resume, or database mutation before execution.
Keep API keys in environment variables and avoid placing secret values in prompts or workflow notes.
Fetch the latest graph, preserve node IDs, validate changes, and re-fetch after every update.
anti_patterns: Do not paste KAPSO_API_KEY or OAuth secrets into chat messages.
Do not change existing node IDs or skip lock version checks during graph updates.
Do not run delete, deploy, force status, resume, or row mutation commands without explicit approval.

faq.question: What does this skill help automate?
faq.answer: It helps plan and run Kapso workflow tasks for WhatsApp triggers, graph edits, executions, functions, integrations, and databases.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include the required helper scripts?
faq.answer: The scanned package only includes SKILL.md. Users need the referenced scripts and dependencies from a trusted source.

faq.question: Does it need credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. It expects KAPSO_API_BASE_URL and KAPSO_API_KEY to be configured as environment variables.

faq.question: Can it change production workflows?
faq.answer: Yes, if connected to production credentials and scripts. Review every mutating action before execution.

faq.question: Can it manage WhatsApp templates or onboarding?
faq.answer: No. The skill points users to a related integrate-whatsapp skill for onboarding, webhooks, messaging, templates, and flows.
